blueprints.title: The code array and the frame it runs in

clauses.text: An instruction is a one byte opcode followed by zero or more operands, an operand wider than one byte is stored big endian, and the instruction stream is aligned to one byte, with `tableswitch` and `lookupswitch` the only two instructions padded so that some of their operands land on a four byte boundary .

A frame is created on each method invocation and destroyed when that invocation completes, normally or abruptly, and it holds its own local variable array, its own operand stack and a reference to the run-time constant pool of the class of its method .

The local variable array is indexed from zero, one entry holds an `int`, a `float`, a `reference` or a `returnAddress`, and a `long` or a `double` occupies two consecutive entries named by the lesser index and required to be aligned to nothing .
The operand stack is last in, first out, is empty when its frame is created, and has a maximum depth that is fixed before the frame exists and supplied with the code .
Each thread has its own pc register, which holds the address of the instruction being executed when the current method is a Java method and holds nothing defined when the current method is native .
`code_length` is greater than zero and less than 65536, so a code array is never empty and never larger than a `u2` can measure, whatever the width of the field that carries it .
Only instructions the specification documents may appear in a code array, the opcodes it reserves may not, and `jsr`, `jsr_w` and `ret` may not appear at class file version 51.0 or above .

The first instruction begins at index 0, each instruction except the last begins at the index of the previous one plus that instruction's length including its operands, and the last byte of the last instruction is the byte at `code_length - 1` .
The operand stack has the same depth at an instruction on every execution path that reaches it, never grows deeper than `max_stack`, and is never popped when empty .
The two local variables holding a `long` or a `double` are never reversed, never split and never operated on individually, and no local variable is read before it has been assigned .

If a constraint stated in an instruction's own description is not satisfied at run time, the behaviour of the machine is undefined, and it is verification at link time that makes this unreachable rather than any check the instruction performs .

Invoking a method whose `ACC_SYNCHRONIZED` flag is set enters a monitor, and that monitor is exited whether the invocation completes normally or abruptly, including when the exception is on its way out of the method .

Normal completion restores the invoker's frame with its pc advanced past the invocation instruction and the returned value, if there is one, pushed onto the invoker's operand stack , and abrupt completion returns no value to the invoker at all .

Enforcing structured locking, meaning that every monitor exit in a method matches an earlier entry in that method, is permitted and not required, so a machine that refuses unstructured locking and a machine that allows it both conform .

A method's bytecodes are stored immediately after the end of the `ConstMethod` that describes them , so the address of the code array is computed from the address of the header rather than stored , and a bytecode pointer is a raw address into metaspace rather than an index.
The code size is held in a `u2` , which makes the specification's bound of less than 65536 a property of the representation here and not a check that could be relaxed.
`max_stack`, `max_locals` and the size of the parameter block are stored beside it in the same width  , so the frame's dimensions are known from six bytes of the method's header.

The interpreter's frame keeps its bytecode pointer and a pointer to its locals as ordinary slots in the frame , which makes both of them per frame values in an implementation whose specification gives the pc to the thread.
The expression stack sits at the machine stack pointer and grows toward lower addresses , so a push moves down through memory while every picture of an operand stack draws it moving up.

The locals and the caller's outgoing arguments are the same words: the argument block the caller assembled becomes the callee's first locals, at the far end of the frame beside the caller's stack pointer , so an invocation does not copy its arguments anywhere.
Bytecode is not immutable, and the flag that permits this says as much in the text it prints to anybody who asks the machine what its options are .

A second and separate kind of rewriting fuses common pairs of instructions into one, under its own flag , and both flags are platform dependent, so their default is a property of the port rather than of the product.

The link time rewrite happens once per class and its main work is replacing constant pool indices in the code array with indices into a constant pool cache , so the operand bytes of a resolving instruction in a running method do not hold the number the class file held.

A class whose `invokespecial` instructions on interfaces overflow the rewriter's own index space is refused with an `InternalError` saying the class file cannot be loaded , which is a refusal of a class file that violates no constraint the specification states.
The pair fusing rewrite happens while the method is executing: the template for `aload_0` reads the following opcode and stores a fused opcode over the `aload_0` it is currently executing .
Every in place patch is guarded by a flag test at the top of the patcher , so an implementation that turns the flag off has a code array that is constant from the moment the class is linked.

The fused and fast forms are numbered above every opcode the specification names and each one records the instruction it was rewritten from , which is what lets a tool map an executing method back onto the class file it came from.

When the instruction after an `aload_0` is a `getfield` that has not itself been rewritten yet, the fusing is deferred rather than done , so which fused instruction a method ends up holding is a function of the order in which its paths first ran.
The pc is calculated and the opcode fetched, then the operands are fetched, then the action is performed, and the number and size of the operands are known only once the opcode is .

A frame exists for the whole of its invocation and no longer: the invoker's frame is not resumed until the callee's is gone, which is what makes the return value arrive on the invoker's stack rather than on the callee's .
A monitor entered by a synchronized method's invocation is exited before an exception leaves that method, so an implementation may not unwind first and release afterwards .

Verification of a class's methods happens before those methods are rewritten, and both happen before the methods are linked  , so the verifier sees the bytes the class file carried and never sees a rewritten one.

All three of those happen while the thread holds the class's own initialization lock , and the class is marked linked only afterwards , which is the whole reason the link time rewrite needs no atomicity.

The in place fusing happens only after the link time rewrite has finished, because it writes opcodes that name a constant pool cache the first rewrite created , so an implementation cannot fuse first and resolve later.

checklist.requirement: decodes a code array from index 0 by instruction length, reads multi byte operands big endian, pads `tableswitch` and `lookupswitch` operands to a four byte boundary measured from the start of the array, and ends the last instruction at `code_length - 1`.

creates one frame per invocation with its own locals, its own operand stack and its own constant pool reference, and destroys it before the invoker resumes, which is checked by walking the stack from inside a recursion.
addresses a `long` or a `double` in the local variable array by the lesser of its two indices, at both even and odd indices, and neither requires nor assumes alignment of the pair.
starts every frame with an empty operand stack and executes correctly a method whose stack reaches exactly `max_stack` on some path, including a `long` or `double` value at the top of it.

gives each thread its own program counter, so two threads executing the same method are at independent points in it, which is checked with two threads in one loop rather than by reading any diagnostic.
executes a method whose code array is one byte long and one whose code array is 65535 bytes long, and refuses a class file offering an empty one.
executes every opcode the specification documents and refuses, before execution, any code array containing an opcode it does not document, including a machine's own internal codes if it has any.

documents which of its own checks are performed at run time and which it relies on verification for, since the specification permits either and a reader cannot tell them apart by testing a machine that is correct.

releases the monitor of a `synchronized` method before an exception raised inside it becomes visible to the invoker, checked with `Thread.holdsLock` in the invoker's handler rather than after the stack has unwound further.
pushes the returned value onto the invoker's operand stack on normal completion and pushes nothing on abrupt completion, checked for each of the five return instructions and for a `void` method.
documents whether it enforces structured locking, and behaves the way it documents for a method that exits a monitor it did not enter and for one that exits two monitors in entry order.
documents any limit its own representation of a method imposes beyond the limits section 4a states, and imposes none that is smaller.

passes arguments to an invoked method so that they arrive as its first local variables in index order, whatever the direction its stacks grow, checked with a method of eight parameters of mixed widths.
produces identical observable behaviour for every program with each of its code rewriting options on and off, which is the item that makes rewriting an implementation detail rather than a semantic.

keeps any rewritten operand meaningful only inside the machine, so that reflection, the class file API and any agent see the constant pool index the class file carried and not the rewritten form, and performs no rewrite that depends on a structure it has not yet built.
loads and executes every class file that satisfies section 4a, or documents each internal limit that makes it refuse one, since a refusal here is a refusal of a legal program.

modifies a code array while threads execute it only by single byte stores after which the instruction sequence beginning at that byte has the same effect and the same end index as before, and reports the original instruction, not the rewritten one, through every interface a program can reach.
determines the length of an instruction from its opcode alone, so that no operand of any instruction is fetched before the opcode that gives it meaning.
verifies a class's methods before transforming them in any way, and makes the class available to other threads only after both have finished, so no thread can execute a partly transformed method.

clauses.text: The first four bytes are the magic number `0xCAFEBABE`, and a file whose first four bytes are anything else is not a class file .

A representation whose major or minor version the implementation does not support is refused with `UnsupportedClassVersionError`, which is a subclass of `ClassFormatError` and exists so that this one cause can be told apart from the rest .

`constant_pool_count` is one greater than the number of entries, the table is indexed from 1 to `constant_pool_count - 1`, and an index is valid only if it is greater than zero and less than the count .

Format checking establishes that the magic number is right, that every predefined attribute has the length its definition gives it, that the file is neither truncated nor followed by extra bytes, and that the constant pool satisfies the constraints stated for it, and it establishes nothing about whether the classes and members named actually exist .
An attribute the implementation does not recognise is ignored in silence, and an implementation is prohibited from refusing a class file because it contains one .

A representation that is not a `ClassFile` structure is refused with `ClassFormatError`, and one that is well formed but names a class other than the one requested, or has `ACC_MODULE` set, is refused with `NoClassDefFoundError` .
Every bit of `access_flags` that Table 4.1-B does not assign is reserved, should be zero in a generated class file, and should be ignored by an implementation reading one .
An interface has `ACC_ABSTRACT` set and `ACC_FINAL`, `ACC_SUPER`, `ACC_ENUM` and `ACC_MODULE` clear, and a class that is not an interface does not have both `ACC_FINAL` and `ACC_ABSTRACT` set .

The bytes of a `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` are modified UTF-8 rather than UTF-8, so no byte may be zero and no byte may lie in the range `0xf0` to `0xff`, and a character outside the basic multilingual plane is encoded as a surrogate pair of three byte sequences .

The format's own field widths are its limits: 65535 constant pool entries, 65535 fields, 65535 methods, 65535 direct superinterfaces, 65535 local variables and 65535 operand stack slots in one frame, and 255 method parameters counted with `long` and `double` as two each .

A class file that does not satisfy the static and structural constraints on the code of a method is refused with `VerifyError`, which is a different error from the one a malformed file gets and is raised at a different point in the class's life .

The magic number is checked before anything else is read, and the message names the value it found in decimal rather than in hexadecimal, so a file starting with the letters `PK` is reported as `Incompatible magic value 1347093252` .
The version is checked even when every other format check has been turned off, which makes it the one property of a class file that cannot be waved through .

A major version below the minimum and a major version above the maximum produce two differently worded errors, `was compiled with an invalid major version` for the first and `has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime` for the second, and only the second one names the version this runtime does support .

A minor version of 65535 is accepted only when the major version is exactly this runtime's own and `--enable-preview` was given, and any other non zero minor version at a major version of 56 or above is refused outright .

Class access flag bits that are not recognised are masked off as the two bytes are read, before any check looks at them, so a class file with reserved bits set loads and the bits are gone by the time anything could object to them .

How much of the class file is checked at all is decided per class from the defining loader and a pair of diagnostic flags, so two identical byte arrays loaded by two different loaders are not held to the same standard .

A JVMTI agent that has registered for the class file load hook forces full checking on regardless of the loader, which means attaching an agent can turn a class file that loaded yesterday into a `ClassFormatError` today .

The argument count of a method is checked against its `max_locals` in the parser, immediately after the two numbers are read and before the code array, and the error is a `ClassFormatError` saying `Arguments can't fit into locals` .
The code array is bounded at 65535 bytes by a check rather than by a field width, and the check runs only when the class is being format checked, so the bound is not enforced for every class .
A class defined from a `byte[]` is parsed from a private copy taken before the machine is called, so a concurrent write to the array cannot affect the class that results .
A class defined from a direct `ByteBuffer` by a platform class loader is parsed in place, out of the caller's own memory, with no copy anywhere between the call and the parser .

An attribute whose name is not recognised is skipped by its declared length, which is the same code path in a class, a field, a method and a `Code` attribute, and an attribute length that runs off the end of the file is caught by the stream rather than by the attribute reader .
Running out of bytes anywhere produces one error with one message, `Truncated class file`, which names neither the structure being read nor the offset it stopped at .
The constant pool is allocated at the count the file declares, before a single entry has been read, which is safe only because the count is bounded at 65535 by its field width .

The stack map frames of a method are validated against that method's `max_stack` while the attribute is being read, and a frame that exceeds it is reported through the verifier's class format error path, which is why breaking `max_stack` produces a `ClassFormatError` naming a rule about type array sizes .

The header is read in the order the structure declares it, magic then minor version then major version then the constant pool count, and no later item may be read before an earlier one, because the earlier ones decide how the later ones are interpreted .

The whole constant pool is read before any index into it is resolved, because an entry may refer to an entry that comes after it, and an implementation that checks references as it reads will reject valid class files .

The error for an unrecognised constant pool tag is held back until the access flags have been read and checked, because a file with `ACC_MODULE` set has to fail with `NoClassDefFoundError` rather than with `ClassFormatError`, and the tag error would otherwise get there first .

The two failures that belong to the loader rather than to the bytes come first: a loader already recorded as an initiating loader of this name fails with `LinkageError`, and a derivation already in progress for this name fails with `ClassCircularityError`, both before the representation is parsed .
Format checking is complete before verification begins, because verification is part of linking and linking happens to a class that already exists .
The check that no bytes remain is last, after every attribute of the class has been read, so an implementation cannot report the extra bytes until it has consumed everything it recognises .

checklist.requirement: refuses every input whose first four bytes are not `0xCAFEBABE`, including the empty input and an input of fewer than four bytes, and does so before interpreting anything else.

accepts exactly the major versions it documents, refuses the ones below and above with `UnsupportedClassVersionError`, and treats a minor version of 65535 as a preview class file rather than as an ordinary one.

indexes the constant pool from 1 to `constant_pool_count - 1`, resolves an entry that refers to a later entry, and does not allocate on the declared count in a way that a count of 65535 with no entries behind it can exhaust.
refuses a truncated file and a file with bytes after the last class attribute, and reaches the second decision only after every attribute it recognises has been consumed.
loads a class carrying an attribute with an unrecognised name on the class, on a field, on a method and inside a `Code` attribute, and reports no error and no warning for any of the four.

distinguishes the three failures of derivation, `ClassFormatError` for a representation that is not a `ClassFile` structure, `NoClassDefFoundError` for one that names a different class or has `ACC_MODULE` set, and reaches the second of those even when the file also contains a constant pool tag it does not recognise.
loads a class file with reserved `access_flags` bits set, and whatever it does with those bits, reports them consistently through every interface it offers.
refuses `ACC_INTERFACE` without `ACC_ABSTRACT`, `ACC_FINAL` together with `ACC_ABSTRACT` on a class, and every contradictory flag pair Table 4.1-B forbids on a field and on a method.
refuses a `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` containing a zero byte or a byte in the range `0xf0` to `0xff`, and accepts a supplementary character encoded as a surrogate pair of two three byte sequences.

accepts a class at each of the format's stated limits, 65535 fields, 65535 methods and 65535 superinterfaces, and refuses a method whose code array exceeds 65535 bytes whatever the width of the field says.

reports a violation of a static or structural constraint on a method's code as `VerifyError` rather than as `ClassFormatError`, which is the item the pinned HotSpot build fails for `max_stack` and for the argument count against `max_locals`.
documents, for every configuration it offers, which checks are skipped, and either performs every 4a check in every configuration or names the configuration in which it does not.

derives, for every entry point that takes a buffer the caller can still write to, a class that some single snapshot of that buffer would have derived, or documents that the entry point is unsafe under concurrent modification.

terminates on every input without reading outside the buffer it was given, which is checked by a fuzzer rather than by a test, and reports a diagnosable error for each of the eight top level items a file can be truncated inside.
reads magic, then minor version, then major version, then the constant pool count, and does not decide anything about a later item before an earlier one has been read.

raises `LinkageError` for a loader already recorded as an initiating loader of the name and `ClassCircularityError` for a derivation already in progress, both before any byte of the representation is parsed.
completes format checking before verification begins, so a class whose bytes are well formed and whose code does not verify exists as a `Class` object before the `VerifyError` is raised.

clauses.text: Every entry begins with a one byte tag, the tag alone decides the structure of the entry and therefore how many bytes follow it, and an entry whose tag is not one of the defined values cannot be skipped because its length is unknown .

A `CONSTANT_Long_info` or a `CONSTANT_Double_info` occupies two consecutive entries in the table, the next usable entry follows at the index after next, and the index in between is unusable and must be considered invalid .

Whether a tag may appear in a pool at all depends on the class file version: `CONSTANT_MethodHandle`, `CONSTANT_MethodType` and `CONSTANT_InvokeDynamic` from 51.0, `CONSTANT_Module` and `CONSTANT_Package` from 53.0, and `CONSTANT_Dynamic` from 55.0 .

Whether `ldc`, `ldc_w` or `ldc2_w` may push an entry depends on the class file version as well, and the thresholds are not the same ones: `CONSTANT_Class` becomes loadable at 49.0, `CONSTANT_MethodHandle` and `CONSTANT_MethodType` at 51.0, `CONSTANT_Dynamic` at 55.0, and the five that were loadable from the beginning at 45.3, so a tag that may legally sit in a pool is not thereby a tag an instruction may load .

The `length` of a `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` is a count of bytes rather than of characters and is two bytes wide, so the longest representable string is 65535 bytes of modified UTF-8 and a string of 65535 characters may have no representation at all .

Nothing in a `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` says what it is for, and a class name, a field descriptor, an attribute name and the text of a string literal are the same structure, so an implementation determines the role of a string from the entry or attribute that names it and never from the string itself .

A `CONSTANT_Fieldref_info` names a class or interface type that has the field, a `CONSTANT_Methodref_info` names a class type and not an interface type, and a `CONSTANT_InterfaceMethodref_info` names an interface type and not a class type, which is why the same reference to the same member is two different tags depending on what declares it .

A `CONSTANT_NameAndType_info` pairs a name with a descriptor and the descriptor decides which names are legal: with a field descriptor the name is an unqualified name, and with a method descriptor it is an unqualified name or one of the two special names, so neither half can be checked without reading the other .

A `CONSTANT_MethodHandle_info` has a `reference_kind` in the range 1 to 9, and the kind decides which entry kinds `reference_index` may name, with kinds 6 and 7 permitted to name a `CONSTANT_InterfaceMethodref_info` only from class file version 52.0 and kind 8 requiring the name to be `<init>` .

A `CONSTANT_Dynamic_info` or a `CONSTANT_InvokeDynamic_info` holds an index into the `BootstrapMethods` attribute rather than into the constant pool, so it is the one entry kind whose first field is not a pool index and a class containing either has to carry that attribute .

The pool is not required to be free of duplicates, so two entries may denote the same constant and an implementation must accept a class file in which they do, which means entry identity is never constant identity .
A `CONSTANT_Module_info` or a `CONSTANT_Package_info` may appear only in the class file of a module declaration, and neither may be the target of any index from any other entry .

The run time constant pool is derived from the class file pool at class creation, its symbolic references are resolved on first use rather than at creation, and an unresolved reference is not an error until something needs it .
If resolution of a symbolic reference fails, every later attempt to resolve that same reference fails with an error of the same class as the first one, and the reference is never re-resolved .

The tag byte in memory has eight values no class file may contain, all of them at 100 or above while the format stops at 20, so an implementation tag and a format tag cannot collide and the same byte can carry both .

Four entry kinds can fail to resolve and each gets its own error tag rather than one shared error state, so an entry that failed still says which kind it was and therefore what the second attempt has to throw .

Which entries are loadable is answered by a comparison against the tag alone, with no version anywhere in it, and the answer includes the implementation tag for an unresolved class as well as the format tags .

The type checking verifier checks `ldc` against a fixed mask of seven tags built without reference to the class file version, on the stated grounds that the parser has already dealt with the method handle kinds .

The only code in the machine that ties loadability to the class file version is the inference verifier written in C, which adds `CONSTANT_Class` to the loadable set at major version 49 and the two method handle kinds at 51 .

That verifier is reached only for a class whose major version is below 50, so the version dependent rule is enforced for exactly the versions where it differs from the version independent one, and the arrangement is correct because 49 is less than 50 rather than because anything checks that it is .

A tag the version does not allow is refused while the entry is being read, with one message that names the tag number and the class file for both the method handle threshold and the dynamic constant one .

A `CONSTANT_Module` or a `CONSTANT_Package` at a version that allows the tag is not refused where it is found: it is recorded, its two bytes are consumed, and parsing continues so that the access flags can be read and the failure reported as a missing class rather than as a malformed one .
Any other tag ends the parse where it stands, with a message that gives the tag as a decimal number and does not give the index it was found at .

The second slot of an eight byte constant is left holding the invalid tag and the second pass checks that it is still invalid, which catches a pool whose entries overlap, and the message names the second index rather than the first one .

An eight byte constant at the last index is refused by a bounds check written as part of reading the entry rather than by the loop, because the loop is about to advance past the end and would not notice .

Whether the bytes of a `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` are checked for modified UTF-8 legality at all is decided per class by the same setting that decides the rest of format checking, so a class file with a zero byte inside a string is refused from one loader and accepted from another .

Every `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` becomes an interned `Symbol` in a table shared by every class in the machine, so the pool stores a pointer rather than the bytes and two classes with the same string share one copy of it .

The cross index checks on member references and on `NameAndType` entries are conditional on format checking as well, so an index that names an entry of the wrong kind is an error for some loaders and not for others .

The version condition on method handle reference kinds 6 and 7 is enforced, and the message it fails with says that the target is not a method and never mentions a version, so the one error a reader is most likely to meet from a class file compiled for an older target names the wrong cause .
A `reference_kind` outside 1 to 9 ends the parse with a message that does give the index, which makes it the one pool error in this list whose message locates itself .

A `CONSTANT_Class` and a `CONSTANT_String` are stored under implementation tags during the first pass and rewritten in the second, so an entry that a reader would call resolved has been through two internal kinds before the class exists .
Every read of a tag is an acquire load and every write of one is a release store, which is what makes the tag the thing that publishes the entry it describes rather than a byte beside it .

The error tag is installed with a compare and swap rather than a store, and a thread that loses that race to a thread which resolved the entry successfully discards its own pending exception and uses the resolved class, so two threads reaching the same failing entry can get two different outcomes .
The class file version is known before any entry is read, because the tag alone decides the length of an entry and which tags are legal is a function of the version .

Every entry is read before any index is resolved, because an entry may name an entry that comes after it, and an implementation that checks indices as it reads will refuse class files that every compiler produces .

The error for an unrecognised tag is raised in the first pass and stops the parse there, while the error for a module or package entry is deferred past the access flags, so the second pass runs only when the first found nothing it had to hold back .
Nothing in the pool is resolved while the class file is being read, so a class whose pool names a class that does not exist is created successfully and fails later or not at all .
The contents of an entry are written before the tag that describes them, so a reader that sees a new tag sees a complete entry and never a half filled one .
A use of an entry already in an error state throws before any attempt is made to resolve it again, which is what makes the failure sticky rather than merely recorded .

checklist.requirement: refuses every entry whose tag is not one of the seventeen defined values, at every index including the first and the last, and does not attempt to skip such an entry by any assumed length.
places the entry after an eight byte constant at the index two further on, refuses any index that names the slot in between, and refuses an eight byte constant declared at the last index.

accepts each tag at the lowest class file version that permits it and refuses it at the version below, for all four thresholds, and reports the refusal as a malformed class file rather than as an unsupported version.

refuses an `ldc` of a `CONSTANT_Class_info` at a class file version below 49.0 and accepts it at 49.0 and above, whichever of its verifiers runs, which is the item the pinned HotSpot build passes only because the two version thresholds involved happen not to overlap.

accepts a `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` of 65535 bytes, treats its length as a byte count rather than a character count, and does not truncate or re-encode a string containing a supplementary character on the way in or out.

determines the role of every `CONSTANT_Utf8_info` from the entry or attribute that names it, and never from the bytes, which is checked by presenting the same string as a class name in one class and as a literal in another and observing that both are accepted.

checks that each of the three member reference kinds names a `CONSTANT_Class_info` and a `CONSTANT_NameAndType_info` of the right kinds, and either performs that check in every configuration or names the configuration in which it does not.
refuses a `CONSTANT_NameAndType_info` whose name is special and whose descriptor does not permit it, and reaches that decision after both halves have been read rather than while either is being read.

refuses a `reference_kind` outside 1 to 9, enforces the entry kind each of the nine requires, and permits kinds 6 and 7 to name a `CONSTANT_InterfaceMethodref_info` at class file version 52.0 and above and not below.

refuses a `CONSTANT_Dynamic_info` or a `CONSTANT_InvokeDynamic_info` whose bootstrap method index has no matching entry, including the case where the class carries no `BootstrapMethods` attribute at all.
accepts a pool containing two entries that denote the same constant, at every entry kind, and does not merge them in a way that changes what any index names.

refuses a `CONSTANT_Module_info` or a `CONSTANT_Package_info` outside a module declaration, refuses any index that names one, and reports a file that contains one together with the module access flag as a missing class rather than as a malformed one.
creates a class whose pool names a class, a field or a method that does not exist, and resolves no entry of the pool during creation.
throws an error of the same class on every use of a reference whose resolution failed, for each of the entry kinds that can fail, without attempting the resolution again.

keeps whatever internal states it needs for an entry in a representation no class file can produce, so that no byte sequence in a class file can put an entry into a state parsing alone should not reach.
documents, for every configuration it offers, which checks of section 3 are skipped, and either performs every 4a check in every configuration or names the configuration in which it does not.

if it shares string storage between classes, derives the same class from the same bytes whether or not another class holding the same strings has been loaded first, and exposes no way for one class to observe that another holds a string it holds.

publishes an entry's contents before the kind that describes them, so that no thread observes an entry in a state whose contents are not yet written, and records a resolution failure exactly once however many threads reach it together.
reads the class file version before the first entry and every entry before the first index is resolved, which is checked by presenting a pool whose first entry names its last one.

clauses.text: There may be at most one `StackMapTable` attribute in the attributes table of a `Code` attribute, and it lives on the `Code` attribute rather than on the method, so a method with no code has nowhere to put one .

In a class file of version 50.0 or above, a `Code` attribute with no `StackMapTable` has an implicit stack map attribute equivalent to one whose `number_of_entries` is zero, so the absence of the attribute is a claim that the method needs no frames rather than a claim that it was not checked .
The order of the frames in the `entries` table is significant and each frame relies on the previous one for some of its semantics, so no entry can be read, moved, inserted or removed on its own .

The first stack map frame of a method is implicit and computed from the method descriptor by the type checker, so the entry at index 0 describes the second frame of the method and the attribute never contains the state at bytecode offset 0 .

The bytecode offset at which a frame applies is the previous frame's offset plus `offset_delta` plus 1, unless the previous frame is the method's initial frame, in which case it is `offset_delta` exactly .

The delta encoding is what makes the frames sorted by definition and the `+ 1` is what makes duplicates impossible to write, so a reader obtains both properties from the arithmetic and neither has to be checked separately .

Every frame's offset has to be the offset at which an instruction starts, because merging the frames with the instructions is undefined unless every frame offset has a corresponding instruction offset and the offsets are monotonically increasing .

A verification type is a one byte tag followed by zero or more bytes, and two of the nine carry anything at all: an `Object_variable_info` carries a `u2` index that has to name a `CONSTANT_Class_info`, and an `Uninitialized_variable_info` carries a `u2` offset that has to be the offset of the `new` instruction that created the object .

A `Long_variable_info` or a `Double_variable_info` describes the first of two locations, the second location has verification type `top` and is not written down anywhere, and the first location may not be the highest numbered local variable or the topmost operand stack entry .

The first byte of a frame decides its kind, and for the two commonest kinds it also carries the offset delta: `frame_type` for a `same_frame` and `frame_type - 64` for a `same_locals_1_stack_item_frame`, with no further bytes read in either case .
Tags in the range 128 to 246 are reserved for future use, which is 119 of the 256 values a first byte can hold, and a reserved tag cannot be skipped because a frame carries no length of its own .

A `chop_frame` drops the last k local variables of the previous frame, k is `251 - frame_type` and is therefore 1, 2 or 3, and it is an error if k is larger than the number of local variables the previous frame has .

An `append_frame` adds k local variables, k is `frame_type - 251` and is therefore 1, 2 or 3, the item at index 0 is the first additional local variable, and an item that is a `Long_variable_info` or a `Double_variable_info` advances the local variable index by two rather than one .

It is an error for any entry of `locals` to represent a local variable whose index exceeds the method's maximum, or for any entry of `stack` to represent a stack entry beyond the method's maximum operand stack size, and the rule is stated separately for `append_frame` and for `full_frame` in the same words .

The initial frame's locals are the `this` type where there is one, followed by the argument types with every two location type followed by `top`, padded with `top` to the method's declared width, and its operand stack is empty .

Nothing requires a frame to be written in the smallest kind that could express it. A `full_frame` may appear anywhere, a `same_frame_extended` may be used wherever a `same_frame` would do, there is no canonical form and no shortest form rule, and a class file that takes the longer option everywhere is legal .

The reserved range has a name in HotSpot and none in the specification: `RESERVED_START` and `RESERVED_END` sit in the same enum as the seven frame kinds, and that enum is the only place either boundary of the range is a constant rather than a sentence .

The attribute is not decoded while the class file is read. Its bytes are bounds checked against `attribute_length` and copied verbatim, and nothing inside it is looked at until the verifier asks for a frame .

A `StackMapTable` whose `attribute_length` is zero is dropped where it is found and the method records no attribute, so a file that declares the attribute and gives it no `number_of_entries` field is accepted and behaves as one with no attribute at all .

A `StackMapTable` in a class file below major version 50 is not recognised as one: the test that matches the attribute name is guarded by the version, so those bytes fall through to the branch that skips attributes nobody knows and are never read again .
Two `StackMapTable` attributes in one `Code` attribute end the parse with a message that names the class file and does not name the method or the attribute index .

The decoder reads the `u2 offset_delta` before it decides whether the frame type is reserved, so on a reserved first byte it has consumed two bytes it had no business reading, and what saves it is that the next thing it does is throw .

There is a second reserved frame type error at the bottom of the same function and it is unreachable, because the branches above it cover 0 to 63, 64 to 127, everything below 247, 247, 248 to 251, 252 to 254 and 255, which is every value a `u1` can hold .

The exception for the first entry is not written once. Each of the five branches that can decode the first entry carries its own pair of assignments, one for the first frame and one for every other, selected by a flag the branch then clears .

The first entry copies the initial frame's locals rather than aliasing them, on the stated grounds that the verifier updates that array in place, so the frame the type checker computed survives being read past .

A frame whose offset is past the end of the code, or which does not land on the first byte of an instruction, is reported as a verify error rather than a format error, and the test is a lookup in a byte array the verifier filled in while walking the code .

`number_of_entries` is compared against the number of frames actually decoded twice, once before each frame as a floor and once at the end for equality, and the two failures give the same message, so a count that is too small and a count that is too large are indistinguishable in a log .

A chop counts local variables and not locations. It walks backwards through the previous frame's expanded array and steps two positions rather than one whenever it lands on the second half of a category 2 value .

A chop that would run off the front of the locals array returns a negative length, which is caught by the same bounds check that catches a frame wider than the method's maximum, so the specification's separate error for chopping too far arrives with the message for an array of the wrong size .

After a chop the frame's flags are recomputed from the surviving locals rather than inherited from the previous frame, because the local variable holding `uninitializedThis` may be one of the ones that was dropped .

An append frame's locals array is allocated at two positions per appended item before any item is read, and a full frame's arrays the same way, because the decoder cannot know which items are category 2 until it has read them .

The second location of a category 2 value is materialised as a verification type of its own, under two names from an enum whose comment says these are not found in class files, and the six values that enum holds begin at 9, above the eight the format defines, so a verifier type can never be mistaken for a file type .

A tag below 6 becomes a verification type by table lookup with no range check of its own, which is safe because the table covers every value below 6, and only a tag above the largest defined one reaches the error .

An `Object_variable_info` whose index is out of range, or which names an entry that is neither a resolved nor an unresolved class, is a stack map format error, while an `Uninitialized_variable_info` whose offset does not point at a `new` instruction is a class format error raised through the verifier rather than through the stream, so two malformations of the same kind arrive by two different routes .

Whether the attribute is read at all is decided per class from the defining loader, by the same pair of flags that decides the rest of verification, so a class from the boot loader in a default configuration has its stack map copied into memory and never decoded .

At major version 50 exactly, a class the type checking verifier rejected with a verify error or a class format error is handed to the inference verifier, which ignores the attribute entirely, so an attribute that fails every check in section 3 can still produce a class that loads and runs  .

The class file version is known before the attribute is recognised, because below major version 50 these bytes are an attribute nobody knows and at 50 and above they are a stack map, and nothing but the version field distinguishes the two .

The method's maximum locals and maximum operand stack size are known before the first frame is decoded, because every frame is checked against both as it is built and neither can be inferred from the attribute .

The code array has been walked before the frames are decoded, because a frame's offset is checked against the set of instruction starts and an `Uninitialized_variable_info`'s offset against the presence of a `new` at that offset, and neither question can be answered from the bytes of the attribute .

The initial frame is computed before the first entry is read, and the first entry is a delta against it, so a reader that starts at the first entry with an empty frame is wrong for every method that takes an argument and right for every method that takes none .

Each frame is complete before the next one begins, because the next frame's locals, its operand stack and its offset are all expressed relative to it, so there is no order in which the entries can be decoded other than the order they are written in .

A failure inside the attribute does not necessarily end the load where it is raised. It is reported through the verifier's error mechanism rather than by throwing, and that mechanism may return so that the class can be offered to a second verifier, which is a possibility every step of section 3 has to tolerate .

checklist.requirement: refuses a `Code` attribute carrying two `StackMapTable` attributes, whether or not the second one is empty, and accepts a `Code` attribute carrying one.

treats a `Code` attribute with no `StackMapTable`, at class file version 50.0 and above, as having one with no entries, and states whether it also accepts an attribute whose `attribute_length` is zero, which the structure does not describe.

decodes the entries in the order they are written, produces different frames when two adjacent entries are exchanged, and does not accept a file in which an entry has been removed without the count changing.

computes the initial frame from the method descriptor and the access flags before reading any entry, places `this` first for an instance method and `uninitializedThis` first for a constructor, follows every `long` and `double` argument with `top`, pads to the declared width with `top`, and starts with an empty operand stack.

applies `offset_delta` exactly for the first entry and `offset_delta + 1` for every other one, which is checked by presenting a method whose first entry has a non zero delta and a second entry with delta zero, and produces frames in strictly increasing offset order without sorting them.

refuses a frame whose offset is past the end of the code array and a frame whose offset falls inside an instruction rather than at its start, and reaches both decisions before the frame is used for anything.

refuses an `Object_variable_info` whose index is out of range or names an entry that is not a `CONSTANT_Class_info`, and an `Uninitialized_variable_info` whose offset is out of range or does not name a `new` instruction, in all four cases.

treats a `Long_variable_info` or a `Double_variable_info` as occupying two locations of which only the first is written, refuses one that is the highest numbered local or the topmost stack entry, and counts local variables rather than locations when a `chop_frame` drops one.

takes the offset delta of a `same_frame` from the first byte and of a `same_locals_1_stack_item_frame` from the first byte minus 64, consuming no further bytes for either, and accepts a class file in which every frame is written as a `full_frame`, producing the same frames it would from the compressed forms.
refuses every first byte in the range 128 to 246, at every position in the attribute including the first and the last, and does not attempt to skip such a frame by any assumed length.

drops the last one, two or three local variables for a `chop_frame` and adds one, two or three for an `append_frame`, advances the local variable index by two for an appended `long` or `double`, and refuses a chop of more local variables than the previous frame has.

refuses a frame whose locals occupy more locations than the method's maximum, or whose operand stack is deeper than the method's maximum, counting locations rather than items so that a frame legal by item count and illegal by location count is refused.

defines a class whose `StackMapTable` contents are arbitrary bytes of the declared length without reading them, and either decodes the attribute for every class or names the configuration in which it does not.
reads the class file version before deciding what the attribute is, and either recognises a `StackMapTable` below major version 50 or ignores it as an unknown attribute, saying which.

does not let a frame produced by `read` alias state that a later caller may modify in place, so that decoding the whole attribute and then walking the frames gives the same answer as decoding and using them one at a time.
refuses an attribute whose `number_of_entries` is smaller than the frames present and one whose `number_of_entries` is larger, and reports the two distinguishably or states that it does not.
recomputes whether a frame holds `uninitializedThis` after a `chop_frame`, rather than inheriting the answer, which is checked by chopping away the only local variable that held it.
accepts every verification type tag from 0 to 8 in both a locals array and an operand stack where the format permits it, and refuses every tag above 8.

states whether a rejected `StackMapTable` ends the load, and if it does not, names the exact set of class file versions for which it does not, so that a conformance run of malformed attributes can be read as a set of refusals rather than as a set of passes.

obtains the method's maximum locals and maximum operand stack size before decoding the first frame, which is checked by lowering `max_locals` in a file whose frames are otherwise valid and observing a refusal.

determines the instruction boundaries of the code array before decoding the frames, which is checked by presenting an `Uninitialized_variable_info` whose offset is a valid instruction offset holding something other than a `new`.

clauses.text: Assignability is reflexive on every verification type, and `top` is a supertype of every other type, so the pairs in which the two types are equal and the pairs whose target is `top` are settled by two rules that load nothing and examine nothing .

Four of the fourteen type terms, `top`, `oneWord`, `twoWord` and `reference`, denote abstract unions of other types and exist to shorten the rules, and no `verification_type_info` can name any of the four, so a class file can present ten of the fourteen and no more .

The primitive verification types reach `top` and nothing else. `int` and `float` are subtypes of `oneWord`, `long` and `double` of `twoWord`, and no rule relates any two of the four, so there is no widening between primitive verification types and `int` to `long` is refused .

Any class or interface type may be widened to any interface type. The rule that says so leaves the source unbound, so no property of the source is consulted, and the specification states the consequence in prose: there is no requirement that a reference stored by a variable of an interface type refers to an object that actually implements that interface .

The soundness of 4a.4 rests outside this relation, on the check `invokeinterface` makes on its receiver every time it runs, so an implementation that accepts what 4a.4 requires and omits that check has built an unsound machine out of a conforming verifier .

A class type widens to another class type when the second names a loaded superclass of the first, and separately when the two carry the same name under two different initiating loaders that resolve to the same loaded class, so a verification type is a name together with a loader and two types with equal names are not necessarily the same type .

An array type widens to exactly three class types, `java.lang.Object`, `java.lang.Cloneable` and `java.io.Serializable`, and only when the class named is the one the bootstrap loader defines, so an array reaches no other interface however many interfaces an array class implements .

Widening between array types is covariant in the component and is defined by a rule that requires the components themselves to widen, and there is no rule for an array whose component is a primitive, so an array of `int` reaches an array of `int` by reflexivity alone and reaches no other array type .

The three uninitialized types are assignable to whatever `reference` is assignable to, and `reference` reaches only `oneWord` and `top`, and no rule makes any of the three assignable to a class type or an array type, so an unconstructed object satisfies no declared reference type at all .

`null` is a subtype of every class type and every array type by two rules of its own, and nothing other than `null` is assignable to `null`, so the relation has a bottom on the reference side and it is not reachable from anywhere else .

The types `byte`, `char`, `short` and `boolean` have no verification type of their own and are all described by `int`, while the array types whose component is one of the four do have verification types of their own, which is the asymmetry that makes 4a.8's silence about primitive components load bearing rather than an oversight .

Widening between references is not reflexive and applies only between two distinct reference types, so it is not the whole relation and an implementation that treats it as the whole relation has lost every pair 4a.1 settles .

Frame assignability is the pointwise lifting of assignability over the locals and over the operand stack, with an explicit check that the two operand stacks have the same length because the stack grows and shrinks, and with the locals lists required to be the same length by the mapping itself .

A frame's flags are either empty or hold the single element `flagThisUninit`, which is present exactly when some local variable holds `uninitializedThis`, and frame assignability requires the source's flags to be a subset of the target's, so a frame in which `this` is unconstructed is not assignable to one in which it is constructed and the reverse is allowed .

A `long` or a `double` occupies two positions in both a locals array and an operand stack, and the two are written in opposite orders: in locals the type comes first and `top` second, and on the stack `top` comes first and the type second, so the pointwise comparison of 4a.13 is over positions and an implementation that compares values has to have expanded them the same way at both ends .

Answering the relation for two distinct reference types requires both classes loaded, and the rules are split between the reference types and everything else so that a query with an atom on either side can be answered without loading anything, which is stated as a goal of the formulation rather than as an optimisation an implementation may skip .

The entry point carries a comment calling itself the whole point of the type system, and its first line is the whole of 3.1: if the two types are equal or the target is the bogus type, the answer is yes before anything else is looked at .

HotSpot's verification types include three query types that no class file can name, and the reference query accepts an uninitialized type as well as a reference, which is what lets one function answer both the questions a frame comparison asks and the questions an instruction's type rule asks .

The four narrow integral component types are verification types in HotSpot and are not in the file format, and an `int` is assignable to each of them, which is the rule that lets a store into an array of `boolean` be accepted .

Every refusal in the relation reaches one of two bare returns with no record of which test failed, which is why the message a refused class produces names two types and a location and never names the rule that refused .

Component assignability is the same function with one difference: the four narrow integral types refuse everything they are not equal to, so an `int` standing in for a `byte` is accepted as a value and refused as an array component .
`null` is assignable to any reference and nothing is assignable to `null`, and both are decided at the top of the reference case before any name is compared and before anything is loaded .

Two reference types with equal names are assignable in both directions and no loader is compared anywhere in the function, so a verification type here is a symbol rather than a name together with a loader, and the question two loaders raise is answered by the loader constraint machinery outside this relation .
Any reference, including any array, is assignable to `java.lang.Object`, decided by comparing the target's symbol against a well known one with neither class loaded .

The interface rule is one `return` statement with a comment over it saying that interfaces are treated as `java.lang.Object`, and the same statement carries the array carve out, so an array reaches an interface only when that interface is `java.lang.Cloneable` or `java.io.Serializable` .

The interface shortcut is skipped in one case, when the access being checked is of a protected member and the source type is `java.lang.Object`, which puts a rule about who may see a member inside the function that answers about types .

The target class is resolved before anything about the pair is decided, so asking whether one type is assignable to another can load a class, can run a user supplied loader, and can fail with a linkage error rather than return an answer .

The source class is loaded only when the target is neither an interface nor `java.lang.Object`, so the commonest reference to reference question in a real class file resolves one class rather than two .

The class to class case is a walk of the source's superclass chain and nothing else, so the interfaces the source implements are never consulted, which they could not usefully be, since every interface target was already answered yes .

While a class data archive is being dumped, an unresolvable pair is recorded as a constraint and the answer is yes without the check being made, so a run that dumps an archive accepts assignments a run that does not would have to resolve, and the check is deferred to the run that uses the archive .

Two array types are compared by component under the rule of 4b.5, and a component that cannot be parsed out of the signature becomes the bogus type rather than an error, which is why the comparison is guarded against a bogus component on either side: without the guard an unparsable component would be assignable to everything  .

The function that turns a class file tag into a verification type handles six tags and calls an abort for everything else, because the two tags that carry a payload are built by the caller out of a constant pool entry or a bytecode offset .

Frame assignability refuses on a locals width mismatch and on an operand stack depth mismatch before comparing a single type, and the two produce different error contexts, so those two failures are distinguishable in a message where the type failures under them are not .

The pointwise comparison returns the index of the first position that refused rather than a set, so a frame with three wrong locals is reported as one wrong local at the lowest index and a person fixing them one at a time gets three rounds of the same message .

Only as many locals as the target declares are compared, on the stated grounds that anything past them is assignable to the bogus type, so a source frame carrying live types beyond the target's declared locals is not refused for carrying them .

The subset test on the flags is a bit test rather than a list operation and it runs last, after every type in both arrays has been compared, so a frame that is wrong in its types and its flags is reported for its types .

Two compile time constants decide which verifier answers and whether its refusal is final, and neither has a flag: the first is 50 and lives in an enum beside three other version boundaries, and the second is 51 and is a macro in the implementation file .
A class below major version 50 is never offered to the type checking verifier, so none of 4b.1 to 4b.20 runs for it and the relation this document describes has no bearing on whether it loads .

The type checking verifier reports failure by returning a symbol rather than by throwing, which is what makes failover possible at all: at major version 50, with no static archive being dumped, a `VerifyError` or a `ClassFormatError` sends the class to the inference verifier, and the only trace outside the log is that the class loaded  .

Whether verification runs at all is decided per class from the defining loader by two flags, so in a default configuration the classes of the runtime image are loaded without this relation being consulted about them once .

The class file major version is known before the relation is consulted for a class, because below one version it is never consulted and at one version a refusal from it is not final, and neither fact can be recovered afterwards .

Both classes are loaded before a pair of distinct reference types that name, `null` and `java.lang.Object` have not already settled can be answered, so the relation cannot be evaluated in an environment that has no loading and cannot be tabulated ahead of the classes it is about .

The target is examined before the source, because whether the target is an interface decides whether the source is loaded at all, and an implementation that resolves the source first has loaded a class it does not need and may throw a linkage error where a conforming machine returns yes .
The shapes of two frames are compared before any of their types, so a frame that is both the wrong width and holding a wrong type is reported for its width and the type is never reached .

The flags are compared after every type, so the two failures cannot both be reported and the type one wins, which is the opposite order from 4c.4 and is worth writing down because an implementation that checks the cheap thing first gets both orders wrong .

The answer for a pair may be produced in one run and checked in another, so the obligation in 4c.2 holds within a single run and not across the two runs an archive spans, and an implementation that caches answers has to know which of the two it is in .

checklist.requirement: answers yes for every type paired with itself and for every type paired with `top`, and reaches both answers without loading any class, which is checked by asking about two class types that do not exist.

accepts every verification type the class file format can express and provides no way for a caller reading a class file to name `top`, `oneWord`, `twoWord`, `reference` or a bare `uninitialized`, so the abstract unions cannot enter through a file.

refuses every ordered pair of two distinct primitive verification types, in both directions, including `int` to `long` and `float` to `double`, and states whether it has narrow integral types of its own and if so that an `int` satisfies one as a value and does not satisfy one as an array component.

accepts a frame declaring a local as an interface the value's class does not implement, accepts an `invokeinterface` through that local, refuses the same frame when the declared type is a class rather than an interface, and throws `IncompatibleClassChangeError` when the call runs rather than allowing the call to dispatch.

states whether a verification type carries a loader, and if it does, distinguishes two class types with the same name under two loaders that resolve to different classes, and if it does not, names where the obligation that they be the same class is discharged instead.

accepts every array type where `java.lang.Object`, `java.lang.Cloneable` or `java.io.Serializable` is expected, refuses every array type where any other interface is expected including one that an array class does implement, and never consults the source's interfaces when the target is a class.

accepts an array of a subclass where an array of a superclass is expected, refuses the reverse, refuses an array of a primitive where any other array is expected, and refuses rather than accepts an array whose component signature does not parse.

refuses `uninitializedThis` and `uninitialized(Offset)` everywhere except against `top` and against themselves, and in particular refuses both against `java.lang.Object`, which is checked by presenting a frame that declares an unconstructed local as `java.lang.Object`.
accepts `null` where any class type or any array type is expected, refuses everything but `null` where `null` is expected, and reaches both without loading the class named on the other side.

accepts a `boolean`, a `byte`, a `short` and a `char` where `int` is expected, since none of the four has a verification type, and refuses an array of any of the four where an array of `int` is expected, since each of those does.

reaches the same answer for a pair of identical reference types as for a pair of identical atoms, without entering the widening rules, and either names the rule that refused in its message or states that it does not.

refuses two frames whose locals arrays differ in width and two whose operand stacks differ in depth, before comparing any type in either, so a frame that is both the wrong width and holding a wrong type is refused for its width.

refuses a frame in which `this` is unconstructed where one in which it is constructed is expected, accepts the reverse, and compares the flags after every type, so a frame wrong in both is refused for its type.

expands a `long` and a `double` into two positions in both a locals array and an operand stack, with the type first in locals and `top` first on the stack, and compares positions rather than values so that a frame legal by value count and wrong by position is refused.

answers a pair with an atom on either side without loading anything, loads only the target when the target is an interface, loads both when both are class types, and propagates the failure to load rather than converting it into a refusal.
accepts a read of a local holding `uninitializedThis` where a reference is expected by an instruction's type rule, or states that it has no query types and answers those questions another way.

states what it does when the access being checked is of a protected member of `java.lang.Object` through a receiver declared as an interface, since this is the one pair for which 4a.4 does not decide the answer on the pinned build.
states whether it ever answers a pair without establishing it, and if it does, names the mechanism that makes the check later and what happens when that later check fails.

states whether a refusal by this relation ends the load, and if it does not, names the exact set of class file versions for which it does not, so that a conformance run of wrong frames can be read as a set of refusals rather than as a set of passes.

reports a frame with three wrong locals in a way whose behaviour is stated, either one position at a time or all three, and accepts a source frame carrying live types at positions past the target's declared locals.

either consults this relation for every class it loads or names the configuration in which it does not, so that a measurement of how often the relation is asked can be read against the set of classes it was asked about.
